text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The first regular Danish Rail (DSB) goods train went through the new Great Belt rail tunnel/bridge fixed link on Sunday between Denmark's two biggest islands - Zealand on which Copenhagen is located and Funen at the mouth of the Baltic. DSB plans to run 40 goods trains per day through the tunnel initially, increasing to 64 per day in June, when passenger rail services are also due to start.

--The weekend saw the placing on the seabed on the Oeresund sound between Denmark and Sweden of the first 20,000-tonne caisson for the bridge section of the fixed road-rail, tunnel-bridge link across the Baltic between the two countries due to be opened in the year 2000.

--An acute dearth of properly trained tax inspectors means that the Danish inland revenue faces difficulties filling 300-600 new posts needed within the coming three years, causing the authorities to consider improving training courses for staff. The Danish Customs & Excuse has ended a major campaign against moonlighting which uncovered millions of crowns worth of tax avoidance.

--For the first time since the setting up of the Danish International Ship Register in 1988, the number of Danish seamen working on Danish commercial vessels fell in 1996 to below 5,000 - a fall of 345 since 1995.

--According to a new survey, 61 percent of Danes believe that economic growth in Denmark would increase through participation in EMU (Europe's economic and monetary union) compared to 63 percent in a previous poll. Denmark opted out of EMU in a 1993 Maastricht referendum.
